WITH staged AS (
    SELECT
        BIKE_ID AS bike_id_raw,
        CRANK_TORQUES AS crank_torques,
        EVENT_DATE AS event_date_source_raw,
        EVENT_TYPE AS event_type_raw,
        HARDWARE AS hardware,
        ISBN AS isbn,
        LAST_CRANK AS last_crank,
        MESSAGE_TYPE AS message_type_raw,
        METADATA AS metadata,
        RIDER_ID AS rider_id_raw,
        TRIP AS trip,
        NULLIF(TRIM(BIKE_ID), '') AS bike_id,
        NULLIF(TRIM(RIDER_ID), '') AS rider_id,
        NULLIF(TRIM(ISBN), '') AS isbn_text,
        NULLIF(TRIM(EVENT_DATE), '') AS event_date_raw,
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(EVENT_DATE), '') AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ) AS event_ts,
        NULLIF(TRIM(EVENT_TYPE), '') AS event_type,
        NULLIF(TRIM(MESSAGE_TYPE), '') AS message_type,
        'ANALYTICS.RAW.TRIP_END' AS source_relation,

            NULLIF(TRIM(EVENT_DATE), '') IS NOT NULL

            TRUE,
            FALSE

    isbn_text_present
FROM staged

Repair attempt (success): all tests passed
Files: ["models/staging/stg_raw_trip_end.sql"]
Diagnosis: The failure is a silver-layer contract violation in four staging models. Review feedback indicates these models are currently projecting helper/raw implementation columns in their final SELECTs, even though the approved implementation_spec allows only a narrower set of output fields per dataset. Investigation confirms this pattern directly in models/staging/stg_raw_trip_end.sql: the model builds a staged CTE with both raw/helper fields and cleaned/typed fields, then the final SELECT exposes all of them, including non-spec columns such as bike_id_raw, event_date_source_raw, isbn, rider_id_raw, and other helper/raw fields. The same issue is reported for the other three staging models: stg_raw_trip_pause exposes columns such as bike_id_raw, isbn_raw, isbn_string_raw; stg_raw_trip_resume exposes bike_id_raw, event_date_source, isbn_raw; and stg_raw_trip_start exposes bike_id_raw, crank_torques_raw, trip_raw. Root cause: the final projections were not constrained to the implementation_spec-approved contract and instead leaked intermediate/raw columns intended only for staging logic. The required fix is to update each affected model so its final SELECT returns only the approved output columns for that dataset, while retaining any helper/raw columns only inside internal CTEs if still needed for transformations.

- Therefore the failure is in `models/staging/stg_raw_trip_end.yml`: it still documents/tests columns that are no longer exposed by the SQL model.
- Similar past repair from vector search confirms the correct action is to align the YAML contract with the final SQL projection, removing or renaming stale raw/helper columns rather than re-exposing them unless intentionally required.
